([[Hudson, North Carolina]]) | draft_year = 2020 | career_start = 2020 | career_end = 2023 | career_number = 15 | career_position = [[Small forward]] | years1 = {{nbay|2020|full=y}} | team1 = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | years2 = 2021 | team2 = →[[Oklahoma City Blue]] | years3 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team3 = [[Maine Celtics]] | years4 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team4 = [[Grand Rapids Gold]] | years5 = [[2023 BAL season|2023]] | team5 = [[Cape Town Tigers]] | highlights = }} '''Joshua Karon Lee Hall''' (born October 8, 2000) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played for Moravian Prep in [[Hudson, North Carolina]] at the [[Postgraduate year|postgraduate level]]. A five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and former [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] commit, Hall chose to forgo [[college basketball]] and immediately enter the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-summer-league-roster-220701|title=Cavaliers Announce 2022 Summer League Roster|publisher=NBA|date=July 1, 2022|access-date=July 4, 2022}} He is a {{convert|6|ft|9|in|adj=on}}, {{Convert|190|lb|adj=on}} [[small forward]]. ==High school career== Hall played his freshman season of high school basketball at [[Southern School of Energy and Sustainability|Southern High School]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]]. For his next two years, he transferred to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]], playing for its local team rather than its prestigious national team. Hall tried out for the national team during his junior season but did not make the team.{{cite web |last=Wertz |first=Langston Jr. |date=June 11, 2019 |title=From an unknown to 5-star recruit? Josh Hall's got a chance. |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article231435678.html |access-date=May 2, 2020 |website=[[The News & Observer]]}} Hall played a [[postgraduate season]] at Moravian Prep in [[Hudson, North Carolina]], averaging 24 points and 4.4 rebounds per game and leading his team to a 34–3 record.{{cite web |last=Pope |first=Jonas IV |date=April 30, 2020 |title=Josh Hall isn't heading to NC State after all. Here are his big plans. |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article242424786.html |access-date=May 2, 2020 |website=[[The News & Observer]]}} At Moravian, he put on 15 pounds of muscle and emerged as a top player in his high school class. Hall was named the North Carolina Player of the Year by scouting service Phenom Hoops.{{cite magazine |last=Friedlander |first=Brett |title=State Signee Josh Hall Named Player of the Year |url=https://www.si.com/college/ncstate/basketball/josh-hall-phenom-hoops-player-of-the-year |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 2, 2020 |date=April 16, 2020}} ===Recruiting=== On November 18, 2019, Hall committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] over offers from [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] and [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]], among others.{{cite magazine |last=Friedlander |first=Brett |title=Five-Star Wing Josh Hall Commits to Wolfpack |url=https://www.si.com/college/ncstate/basketball/five-star-hall-commits |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 1, 2020 |date=November 18, 2019}} By the end of his high school career, he was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and a four-star recruit by [[247Sports]] and [[ESPN]].{{cite web |title=Rivals analyst sees scenario where Josh Hall ends up at NC State |url=https://ncstate.rivals.com/news/rivals-analyst-sees-josh-hall-ends-up-at-nc-state-wolfpack-basketball |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=May 2, 2020 |date=April 8, 2020}} On April 6, 2020, Hall declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Schuster |first=Blake |title=NC State Signee Josh Hall Declares for 2020 NBA Draft, Will Maintain Eligibility |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2885416-nc-state-signee-josh-hall-declares-for-2020-nba-draft-will-maintain-eligibility |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=May 2, 2020 |date=April 6, 2020}} On April 30, he announced that he would remain in the draft and sign an [[sports agent|agent]], forgoing college basketball.{{cite web|date=May 1, 2020|title=NC State recruit Josh Hall to stay in NBA draft, skip college|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29123650|access-date=March 23, ==Professional career== ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2020–2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Hall signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] On December 9, 2020.{{cite web |title=Thunder Signs Moses Brown and Josh Hall to Two-Way Contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/brown-hall-201209 |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 9, 2020 |date=December 9, 2020}} On September 12, 2021, Hall was waived by the Thunder.{{cite web|title=Thunder Waives Josh Hall|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-hall-210912|website=NBA.com|date=September 12, 2021|access-date=September 12, 2021}} ===Raptors 905 (2021–2022)=== Hall was signed to an Exhibit 10 contract by the [[Toronto Raptors]], and was waived to receive a contract to join the [[Raptors 905]].{{Cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=October 13, 2021 |title=Raptors Signing Josh Hall To Exhibit 10 Contract |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/10/raptors-signing-josh-hall-to-exhibit-10-contract.html |access-date=2021-10-14 |website=Hoops Rumors |language=en-US}} ===Maine Celtics (2022)=== On October 24, 2022, Hall joined the [[Maine Celtics]] training camp roster.{{cite web |date=October 24, 2022 |title=Maine Celtics Select Two in G League Draft, Announce Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/maine-celtics-select-two-in-g-league-draft-announce-training-camp-roster/n-5892371 |access-date=October 24, 2022 |website=oursportscentral.com}} However, he did not make the opening-night roster. ===Grand Rapids Gold (2023)=== On February 11, 2023, Hall was acquired by the [[Grand Rapids Gold]]. He was later waived on March 3, 2023.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=February 11, 2023|access-date=February 11, 2023}} === Cape Town Tigers (2023) === On February 23, 2023, Hall was announced by the [[Cape Town Tigers]] of the [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL).{{Cite web |last=Dia |first=Jules |date=February 23, 2023 |title=BAL 2023: Cape Town signe un ancien de la NBA |url=https://sportnewsafrica.com/breve/bal-2023-cape-town-signe-un-ancien-de-la-nba/ |access-date=February 23, 2023 |website=Sport News Africa |language=fr-FR}} He left the Tigers ahead of the [[2023 BAL Playoffs|playoffs]].{{Cite web |date=May 18, 2023 |title=Playoffs rosters confirmed – Who are the new signings heading to Kigali?
